We perform averaged circuit eigenvalue sampling (ACES) to acquire detailed context-dependent error information on all elements of the syndrome extraction process. Furthermore, we leverage soft information produced from measurement devices to augment the decoder with measurement error information and detect leakage errors for exclusion through post-selection. Our noise-informed approach yields up to 38.3\% improvement in the logical error rate of a distance-5 implementation of the dynamic compass code in experiment.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the dynamic compass code, a new subsystem code for quantum error correction, demonstrating improved performance through tailored decoding strategies in superconducting qubit arrays.
AI.motivation: The need for effective quantum error correction in the face of imperfect hardware to enable practical quantum computing.
AI.method: Introduces the dynamic compass code with a specialized syndrome extraction cycle for efficient qubit use on a heavy-hex lattice, along with a detailed noise characterization and augmented decoder using soft information from measurements.
AI.result: Achieved a 38.3% improvement in logical error rates through noise-informed decoding strategies in a distance-5 experiment.
AI.conclusion: The dynamic compass code significantly enhances logical qubit performance by adapting to device-specific noise, proving viable for scalable quantum computing.

title: Exploring non-equilibrium effects in sequential freeze-in
summary: Freeze-in of multi-component dark sectors is governed not only by the interaction with the thermal plasma, but also by their internal dynamics. Full thermalisation within the dark sector is not guaranteed, raising the question of impact of departures from local thermal equilibrium onto the evolution and ultimately relic abundance and momentum distribution of dark matter. In this work we explore this question in a minimal two-scalar model, which can give rise to observable signatures in indirect detection and long-lived particle searches at forward physics experiments. Focusing on the phenomenologically viable regions, we analyse the impact of non-thermal evolution on the dark matter abundance, finding deviations of up to an order of magnitude between the full phase-space treatment and the traditional number-density approach. Our results highlight the importance of phase-space level computation for accurate freeze-in predictions and further motivate dedicated numerical tools for studying the evolution of multi-component dark sectors at the phase space level.

AI.tldr: This study examines the freeze-in process of multi-component dark sectors, emphasizing the significance of their internal dynamics and deviations from thermal equilibrium on dark matter abundance and distributions.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand how non-equilibrium dynamics affect dark matter properties, which is crucial for accurate predictions in dark sector models.
AI.method: They utilize a minimal two-scalar model to analyze the effects of non-thermal evolution on dark matter abundance, comparing a full phase-space treatment with a traditional number-density approach.
AI.result: The study finds deviations in dark matter abundance predictions of up to an order of magnitude, highlighting significant differences between the two analytical methods.
AI.conclusion: The findings underscore the necessity for phase-space level computations in freeze-in scenarios and call for advanced numerical tools to better study multi-component dark sectors.

title: A Generalized Algorithmic Framework for Detecting Faraday Rotation Measure Flares in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts
summary: Variations in the Faraday rotation measure (RM) of repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide critical diagnostics of the dynamically evolving magneto-ionic environments surrounding their progenitors. Sudden, transient ``RM flares'' can trace the passage of discrete magneto-ionic structures, such as stellar coronal mass ejections from the companion or other dense plasma clumps, across the line of sight. However, identifying these rare events is difficult because RM evolution manifests a wide range of complex behaviors, from smooth, long-term trends to chaotic stochasticity, further complicated by highly non-uniform temporal sampling. This complexity makes it a non-trivial challenge to distinguish localized physical flares from intrinsic environmental volatility. We present a generalized algorithmic framework that establishes a statistically robust methodology for the automated detection and characterization of RM flares. By objectively isolating discrete transient perturbations from quiescent backgrounds, this pipeline enables the first uniform census of environmental variability across the FRB population. Applying this framework to 15 repeating FRBs, we find that high-confidence RM flares are remarkably rare, with FRB 20220529A being the only source to exhibit a statistically significant event under standardized parameters. Other active repeaters instead display high-level intrinsic fluctuations or secular evolution. This work provides a rigorous foundation for distinguishing between different modes of local plasma dynamics, offering a crucial diagnostic tool for identifying the diverse progenitor systems and local environments of FRBs.

AI.tldr: This study presents a framework for detecting and characterizing variations in the Faraday rotation measure (RM) of repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs), focusing on identifying rare RM flares amid complex environmental fluctuations.
AI.motivation: Identifying RM variations can provide insights into the magneto-ionic environments of FRBs, but the complexity and variability of RM evolution challenge the detection of transient phenomena.
AI.method: A generalized algorithmic framework is introduced for automated detection of RM flares, distinguishing them from background noise and environmental fluctuations.
AI.result: The application of this framework to 15 FRBs revealed that significant RM flares are rare, with only one source showing a statistically significant event, while others displayed intrinsic variability.
AI.conclusion: The research establishes a foundational tool for analyzing plasma dynamics around FRBs, aiding in the understanding of their progenitor systems.

title: Precision Limits of Multiparameter Markovian-Noise Metrology
comment: 39 pages (17 main text + 22 appendices). Comments and feedback are welcome
summary: Measuring stochastic signals ("noise metrology") constitutes a central task in quantum sensing and the characterization of open quantum systems. Here we establish ultimate precision bounds for multiparameter estimation of stochastic signals encoded through Markovian Lindblad dynamics, allowing for arbitrary quantum control and noiseless ancillae. Although Markovianity enforces standard-quantum-limit scaling with sensing time $T$, our bounds reveal Heisenberg-type scaling in the number of dissipative channels, $R$: when the stochastic signal exhibits high-rank correlations across the $R$ channels and the probe is entangled, the average variance (per parameter) scales no better than $Ω(1/(TR^2))$. For collective $k$-body dissipation, $R=Θ(N^k)$, signifying super-Heisenberg scaling with the system size $N$. We further show that, when the unknown parameters enter through the dissipative eigenrates, a Rapid Prepare-and-Measure (RPM) protocol that tracks many distinct quantum jumps in parallel attains these limits. In this regime, the estimation problem reduces to a multi-Poisson counting model, providing a conceptually clean route to optimal quantum noise metrology. We illustrate the breadth of the framework with applications to networked noise metrology, collective many-body dissipation, learning Pauli noise, and subdiffraction quantum imaging.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes precision bounds for estimating stochastic signals in quantum systems, showing enhanced scaling under specific conditions and proposing a protocol for optimal measurements.
AI.motivation: To advance noise metrology in quantum sensing and characterize open quantum systems effectively.
AI.method: The study formulates ultimate precision bounds for multiparameter estimation using Markovian Lindblad dynamics, focusing on entangled probes and high-rank correlations across dissipative channels.
AI.result: It discovers that for high-rank correlations, average variance scales as Ω(1/(TR²)), revealing super-Heisenberg scaling with system size in collective k-body dissipation scenarios.
AI.conclusion: A Rapid Prepare-and-Measure protocol allows optimal measurement strategies for quantum noise metrology in various applications.

title: Rescattering effects in near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction
summary: We investigate near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction off the nucleon, focusing on hadronic rescattering effects induced by open-charm meson-baryon intermediate states. Beyond the conventional Pomeron-exchange mechanism, the $\bar D^0Λ_c^+$ and $\bar D^{*0} Λ_c^+$ channels are incorporated within an effective Lagrangian framework. The relevant production amplitudes are evaluated at tree level from $t$-, $s$-, and $u$-channel diagrams in a gauge-invariant manner. The resulting total and $t$-dependent differential cross sections are compared with recent near-threshold data from the GlueX, $J/ψ$-007, and CLAS experiments at Jefferson Lab. We find that the open-charm rescattering contributions significantly improve the description of the data, particularly at large momentum transfer, and naturally generate cusp-like structures near the $\bar D^0 Λ_c^+$ and $\bar D^{*0} Λ_c^+$ thresholds in the GlueX data. We further present predictions for the associated open-charm processes $γp \to \bar D^{(*)0} Λ_c^+$, whose cross sections are estimated to be of the order of 5 nb.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction, focusing on hadronic rescattering and open-charm states, showing improved data fitting through effective Lagrangian methods.
AI.motivation: To explore the impact of open-charm meson-baryon intermediate states on $J/ψ$ photoproduction, beyond conventional mechanisms.
AI.method: An effective Lagrangian framework was used to incorporate $ ar D^0Λ_c^+$ and $ ar D^{*0} Λ_c^+$ channels, calculating production amplitudes via tree-level diagrams in a gauge-invariant way.
AI.result: The inclusion of open-charm rescattering significantly enhances data fitting, especially at large momentum transfer, and reveals cusp-like features in GlueX data around thresholds.
AI.conclusion: Predictions for open-charm processes show cross sections around 5 nb, highlighting the relevance of intermediate states in photoproduction.

title: Low-valency scalable quantum error correction with a dynamic compass code
summary: The ongoing development of hardware that is capable of reliably executing general quantum algorithms requires quantum error-correcting codes that are both practical for realisation and rapidly reduce logical error rates as they are scaled up. Here we introduce the dynamic compass code, a code that can be implemented with a modest footprint on the heavy-hex lattice while also demonstrating a threshold. The dynamic code is obtained by choosing a novel measurement schedule for the syndrome extraction circuit of the heavy-hex subsystem code. We numerically evaluate its performance and observe that different choices of schedule can provide a trade-off in protection against logical errors in the $X$ vs $Z$ basis. We also demonstrate that this new measurement schedule provides the code with a threshold for stability experiments. We finally show how the dynamic compass code could be used for fault-tolerant logic by illustrating lattice surgery between code patches.

AI.tldr: The dynamic compass code is a new quantum error-correcting code designed for efficient implementation and improved error rates, evaluated through a novel measurement schedule that balances error protection in different bases while enabling fault-tolerant logic.
AI.motivation: There is a need for practical quantum error-correcting codes that efficiently reduce logical error rates as quantum hardware scales.
AI.method: The dynamic compass code is implemented using a novel measurement schedule for the syndrome extraction circuit of the heavy-hex subsystem code, evaluated numerically.
AI.result: The dynamic compass code offers a balance in protection against logical errors in the $X$ vs $Z$ basis and demonstrates a threshold for stability experiments.
AI.conclusion: This code can facilitate fault-tolerant logic through lattice surgery between code patches.

title: Status of the hadronic light-by-light contribution to the muon $g-2$ and holographic QCD predictions
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Proceedings contribution for the Workshop FCCP2025, Anacapri, Italy, Sep 29 - Oct 1, 2025, to appear in EPJ Web of Conferences
summary: We review the recent progress made with regard to the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) contribution to the Standard Model prediction of the muon anomalous magnetic moment and how well this compares with predictions from holographic QCD models, which had predicted larger contributions from axial vector mesons and short-distance constraints than the White Paper of 2020. A new holographic prediction concerns tensor-meson contributions, which in holographic QCD play a significant role in short-distance constraints beyond the Melnikov-Vainshtein constraint. When matching also the symmetric longitudinal short-distance constraint, the resulting prediction for the tensor-meson transition form factors agree well with available singly virtual data, but lead to different results than the traditional quark-model ansatz and a sizable positive contribution that could explain the remaining current tension between lattice and data-driven results for the HLbL contribution.

AI.tldr: The paper reviews advancements in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment, focusing on holographic QCD models and their predictions concerning tensor-meson contributions.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the HLbL contribution's role in the discrepancy between theoretical predictions and experimental data for the muon anomalous magnetic moment.
AI.method: The paper analyzes holographic QCD models and their tensor-meson contributions, comparing them with the 2020 White Paper's predictions and existing data.
AI.result: Holographic predictions show significant alignment with singly virtual data for tensor-meson transition form factors, presenting a sizable positive contribution to the HLbL estimate.
AI.conclusion: This contribution might resolve the existing tensions between lattice QCD calculations and empirical results regarding the HLbL effect.

title: Glauber-Lachs formula-based analysis of three-pion Bose-Einstein correlation data at 7 TeV from the LHCb Collaboration
summary: We combine the Glauber--Lachs formula from quantum optics and the two-component picture for pion production to analyze data on two- and three-pion Bose--Einstein correlation at 7 TeV from the LHCb Collaboration. For the pion exchange function $E_{\rm 2B}$, we chose a dipole form and an inverse one-and-a-half pole form. The extensions are computed in the configuration space of 4-dimensional Euclidean space ($ξ=\sqrt{|\bm r_1-\bm r_2|^2+(t_1-t_2)^2}$).

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes two- and three-pion Bose–Einstein correlations at 7 TeV using quantum optics and a two-component model for pion production.
AI.motivation: To enhance understanding of pion production and correlations in high-energy collisions, particularly in the context of LHCb data.
AI.method: Utilization of the Glauber–Lachs formula alongside a two-component picture for pion production, employing a dipole form and an inverse one-and-a-half pole form for the pion exchange function $E_{2B}$ in a 4D Euclidean configuration space.
AI.result: The analysis provides insights into the correlations observed in LHCb data, refining the model of pion interactions and production mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: The findings contribute to a deeper comprehension of Bose–Einstein correlations in particle physics, fostering better modeling of high-energy collision events.

title: Cell-Dependent Criticality for Quantum Metrology
summary: Exploiting enhanced sensitivity of a system in the vicinity of a phase transition boundary, critical quantum metrology to date still suffers from gap-closure related bottleneck effects, namely, critical slowing down of the sensing dynamics and a drastic shrinking of the parameter sensing window. To alleviate the said bottleneck inherent to any homogeneous lattice used for sensing, here we propose to leverage the intrinsic hopping inhomogeneity arising from bosonic ladder-operator matrix elements in Fock-space lattices (FSLs). Specifically, using a two-mode Jaynes--Cummings-type model, we show that the sensing parameter can be imprinted onto a topological zero-energy mode of the FSL. The key system parameters thus become cell dependent, effectively tracing out a curve in a topological phase diagram. Cell-dependent criticality emerges when this curve crosses or approaches a topological phase boundary, without globally tuning the lattice close to criticality. An external control parameter reshapes this curve, continuously tuning the scaling of the quantum Fisher information from the standard to the Heisenberg scaling while maintaining broad sensing coverage and a reduced gap cost. Furthermore, a local photon-number measurement on a single cavity saturates the quantum Fisher information. These results identify FSLs as a scalable and practical route to criticality-based quantum metrology.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using Fock-space lattices to enhance quantum metrology near phase transitions, addressing challenges like critical slowing down and parameter sensing limits.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to overcome limitations in critical quantum metrology caused by gap-closure effects near phase transition boundaries.
AI.method: The authors utilize a two-mode Jaynes-Cummings model on Fock-space lattices, focusing on cell-dependent parameters that allow for tuning within a topological phase diagram.
AI.result: The approach enables a continuous transition from standard to Heisenberg scaling of quantum Fisher information and broadens the sensing range while reducing gap costs.
AI.conclusion: Fock-space lattices are put forward as a scalable solution for effective criticality-based quantum metrology.

title: Phenomenology of Vanishing Effective Majorana Mass with a Sterile Neutrino under Cosmological and JUNO Constraints
summary: In the present work we investigate the phenomenological implications of a vanishing effective Majorana neutrino mass within a $3+1$ neutrino framework adding a eV-scale sterile neutrino beside three active neutrino states in light of latest cosmology driven bounds on sum of neutrino masses ($\sum_{i}m_i$). We explore the parameter space where the destructive interference between active and sterile states leads to vanishing amplitude, $M_{ee}$, of neutrinoless double beta ($0νββ$) decay. The allowed parameter space has been identified and predictions have been obtained taking into account the latest Planck and DESI+CMB bound on $\sum_{i}m_i$. We find that these bounds restrict the sterile mixing angle $θ_{14}$ and the lightest active neutrino mass. Furthermore, we incorporate the refined precision data from JUNO experiment regarding solar oscillation parameters ($θ_{12}, Δm_{21}^2$). We find that the sterile neutrino parameters like $θ_{14}$ may not be sensitive to the JUNO precision measurements as the constraint imposed by precise $θ_{12}$ is washed out by new cancellations driven through additional CP violating phases leading to vanishing $|M_{ee}|$.

AI.tldr: This study examines the effects of a zero effective Majorana neutrino mass in a 3+1 neutrino model with a sterile neutrino, focusing on constraints from cosmological bounds and the implications for neutrinoless double beta decay.
AI.motivation: To investigate the implications of a zero effective Majorana mass in the context of a 3+1 neutrino model and understand the parameter space involving sterile neutrinos.
AI.method: Analysis of neutrino mass parameters, interactions, and cancellations between active and sterile states, incorporating cosmological data and JUNO experimental results.
AI.result: Identified parameter space shows that cosmological bounds restrict the sterile mixing angle and the lightest active neutrino mass, with some cancellations arising due to CP violation affecting detection of certain parameters.
AI.conclusion: Sterile neutrino parameters may be less sensitive to precise measurements from the JUNO experiment, indicating complex interactions between neutrino states that challenge straightforward interpretations.

title: Warring Contextualities - Provably Classical vs Provably Nonclassical
summary: In the literature, there are two differing definitions of contextuality: Kochen and Specker's, and Spekkens' (or ``generalised''). However, researchers using one of these definitions rarely consider the other, meaning comparative analysis of these two notions is rare. In this paper, we advance the idea that Kochen-Specker contextuality provides a generalisation of the idea of system being fundamentally nonclassical, while Spekkens' noncontextuality provides a generalisation of the idea of a system being classical. This allows us to reconcile the two approaches, as different stages in a hierarchy of classicality/nonclassicality.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two definitions of contextuality—Kochen-Specker's and Spekkens'—and proposes a hierarchy linking them to classical and nonclassical systems.
AI.motivation: The existing literature lacks comparative analysis of Kochen-Specker and Spekkens' definitions of contextuality, which leads to an incomplete understanding of their relationship.
AI.method: The authors explore the conceptual frameworks of both definitions, arguing that Kochen-Specker contextuality relates to nonclassical systems and Spekkens' noncontextuality relates to classical systems, suggesting a hierarchical structure between them.
AI.result: The paper proposes a reconciliation of the two notions, establishing a framework that positions them as different stages of classicality and nonclassicality.
AI.conclusion: The suggested hierarchy enriches the understanding of contextuality in quantum systems and provides a unified perspective on the classical versus nonclassical nature of systems.

title: Boson sampling beyond the dilute regime: second moments and anti-concentration
summary: Boson sampling is a leading candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage in photonic systems. Despite significant experimental and theoretical progress, a characterization of its output statistics remains incomplete. This is especially true beyond the dilute regime, where photon collisions and bunching become significant. The associated saturated regime, characterized by mode number growing linearly with photon number, or more generally sub-quadratically, is precisely the regime of greatest experimental interest. As a consequence, anti-concentration of the output distribution--a key ingredient in hardness arguments--remains poorly understood in boson sampling. In this work, we leverage representation-theoretic tools to address this gap, obtaining closed-form expressions for second moments of generic particle-number-preserving bosonic observables. We express these quantities in terms of Hilbert-Schmidt norms of projections onto irreducible components of the operator space and show that these projection norms admit compact analytical expressions by exploiting the underlying symmetry structure. Focusing on Fock state output probabilities, we further establish anti-concentration beyond the dilute regime. Together with recent complexity-theoretic results, our findings strengthen hardness guarantees for boson sampling in experimentally interesting settings.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the incomplete characterization of output statistics in boson sampling, especially under conditions involving significant photon interactions. It utilizes representation-theoretic methods to derive expressions for second moments of bosonic observables and establishes anti-concentration results beyond the dilute regime.
AI.motivation: To fill the gap in understanding the output statistics of boson sampling, particularly in the saturated regime where photon interactions are prevalent and critical for demonstrating quantum advantage.
AI.method: The authors leverage representation-theoretic tools to obtain closed-form expressions for second moments of bosonic observables and utilize Hilbert-Schmidt norms to analyze projection onto irreducible components in the operator space.
AI.result: The study establishes closed-form expressions for important statistical quantities and demonstrates anti-concentration in boson sampling beyond the dilute regime, reinforcing the complexity-theoretic results related to hardness guarantees.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide deeper insights into the output distributions of boson sampling, essential for its practical implementation and theoretical validation, especially in regimes of experimental interest.

title: Production of doubly heavy quarkonium associated with two heavy quarks via top quark decays
summary: In this paper, we analyze the $1 \rightarrow 4$ decay channel for the production of doubly heavy quarkonium, $(b\bar{c})$ or $(c\bar{c})$, via top-quark decays, $t \to (b\bar{c}) + c + c + \bar{s}$ and $t \to (c\bar{c}) + b + c + \bar{s}$, within the framework of nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD). The dominant contributions are considered in color-singlet S-wave states, i.e., $(b\bar{c})[^1S_0]$, $(b\bar{c})[^3S_1]$, $(c\bar{c})[^1S_0]$, and $(c\bar{c})[^3S_1]$. Our calculations show that the decay widths for $\bar{B_{c}}$, $\bar{B_{c}^{*}}$, $J/ψ$ and $η_{c}$ production are 0.2251, 0.3099, 0.0537 and 0.0555 MeV, respectively, resulting in ${\cal O}(10^{4}\text{--}10^{6})$ level of $\bar{B}_c^{(*)}$ events and ${\cal O}(10^{3}\text{--}10^{5})$ level of charmonium produced at LHC per year. In particular, we find that the dominant contribution to $J/ψ$ and $η_{c}$ production via top-quark decays arises from this decay channel proposed in this work. Moreover, this multi-body top-quark decay process can serve as a sensitive probe for validating the narrow-width approximation (NWA). Finally, we provide a detailed analysis of theoretical uncertainties and differential distributions to facilitate the corresponding experimental searches. The production of a hadron associated with three quarks contains rich physical information, providing new insights for the LHC to study $B_c$ mesons and charmonia.

AI.tldr: The paper examines the $1 \rightarrow 4$ decay channel for producing $(b\bar{c})$ and $(c\bar{c})$ quarkonium from top-quark decays using NRQCD, presenting calculations for decay widths and potential experimental implications for LHC.
AI.motivation: To explore the production mechanisms of doubly heavy quarkonium states through top-quark decays, enhancing understanding of heavy quark interactions in high-energy physics.
AI.method: Utilizing nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) to analyze the decay channels $t \to (b\bar{c}) + c + c + \bar{s}$ and $t \to (c\bar{c}) + b + c + \bar{s}$, focusing on S-wave color-singlet states and calculating their decay widths.
AI.result: Decay widths calculated for $ ar{B_{c}}$, $ ar{B_{c}^{*}}$, $J/ψ$, and $η_{c}$ yield event predictions on the order of ${\cal O}(10^{4}\text{--}10^{6})$ for $ ar{B}_c^{(*)}$ and ${\cal O}(10^{3}\text{--}10^{5})$ for charmonium production at LHC.
AI.conclusion: The discovered decay channels are significant for producing $J/ψ$ and $η_{c}$, offering insight into quarkonium production and validating the narrow-width approximation, with suggested theoretical and experimental follow-up.

title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
summary: Many combinatorial optimization problems admit a maximin fairness variant, where the aim is to find a distribution over possible solutions which maximizes an expected worst-case outcome. However, the support for an optimal distribution may be exponential, which can be intractable to represent in the worst case. To this end, we propose a quantum based approach to solving distribution optimization problems. Expanding on work analyzing the Dynamical Lie Algebras of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), we show that with a finite number of layers, a QAOA ansatz can be constructed to capture any distribution over bitstrings. We show that the resulting circuit is able to effectively solve the Fair Cut Cover, a fair interpretation of the classical Fractional Cut Cover Problem. In addition, we show that our algorithm is provably better than classical approximations on certain graph structures and empirically outperforms these classical algorithms on tested instances.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a quantum approach to solving maximin fairness distribution optimization problems, demonstrating its superiority over classical methods for specific cases.
AI.motivation: To efficiently tackle maximin fairness optimization problems where optimal distributions can be complex and expansive.
AI.method: A quantum circuit is constructed using a QAOA ansatz that captures distributions over bitstrings with a finite number of layers, specifically addressing the Fair Cut Cover problem.
AI.result: The proposed quantum algorithm shows provable superiority over classical approximations and outperforms them empirically on various graph instances.
AI.conclusion: The quantum approach to distribution optimization enhances efficiency and effectiveness compared to certain classical algorithms, particularly for particular graph structures.

title: Symmetry Preserving Contact Interaction Approaches: An Overview of Meson and Diquark Form Factors
comment: 45 pages, 18 figures, review article. Accepted for publication in Particles (MDPI), 2026
summary:
We present an updated overview of the symmetry preserving Contact Interaction model in hadronic physics, developed a little over a decade ago to describe the mass spectrum and internal structure of mesons and diquarks composed of light and heavy quarks. Over the years, the Contact Interaction has evolved into a framework capable of treating both ground and excited states, providing a simple yet consistent approach to nonperturbative QCD. In this review, we examine the mass spectrum and elastic form factors of forty mesons with different spins and parities, together with their corresponding diquark partners. Importantly, we update the comparison of Contact Interaction predictions using recent results from the literature, offering a fresh perspective on the model's performance, strengths, and limitations. The analysis presented here refines previous conclusions and supports the Contact Interaction as a practical tool for hadron structure studies, with potential applications to baryons and multiquark states. We also present comparisons with other theoretical models and approaches, including lattice quantum chromodynamics, and comment on future prospects in view of ongoing and planned hadron structure experimental programs.
  In particular, forthcoming measurements at FAIR, together with future studies at Jefferson Lab and the Electron Ion Collider, are expected to provide key insights into hadron structure, with FAIR offering indirect constraints via hadron spectroscopy, hadronic interactions, and in-medium properties, while high-precision data on meson structure and form factors from Jefferson Lab and the Electron Ion Collider will provide valuable benchmarks to confront Contact Interaction based predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the evolution and current application of the Contact Interaction model in hadronic physics, focusing on the mass spectrum and form factors of mesons and diquarks, as well as comparisons with experimental results and other theoretical frameworks.
AI.motivation: The motivation for this work is to provide a comprehensive overview of the Contact Interaction model, which facilitates a nonperturbative understanding of QCD and has potential applications in baryon and multiquark studies.
AI.method: The paper employs the Contact Interaction model to analyze the mass spectrum and elastic form factors of various mesons and their diquark partners, incorporating recent literature to update comparisons and refine prior results.
AI.result: The analysis reveals that the Contact Interaction model remains a viable tool for studying hadronic structure, successfully aligning many predictions with recent experimental data while identifying its strengths and limitations.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that ongoing experiments, particularly at FAIR and Jefferson Lab, will enhance our understanding of hadron structure and provide critical benchmarks for testing the Contact Interaction model.

title: Revealing the physical structure of the general quantum master equation
summary: The Lindblad (GKLS) master equation, which represents the mathematical form for the general evolution of a density matrix, is a versatile and widely-used tool in open quantum systems. In contrast with the typical approach of imposing additional conditions on the system, such as weak coupling or energy conservation, we explore the structure of the equation with no assumptions. We demonstrate that general quantum dynamics can be expressed through a combination of free evolution, exchanges of some physical quantities (generalised charges), not necessarily commuting with the Hamiltonian, between the system and the bath, and pure dephasing. This result comprises a novel perspective on quantum master equations, employing physical processes as elemental parts. We use it to explore the dynamics and stationary states of a two-level system and show that strong coupling, particle exchange, and non-Abelian effects all share the same physical origin. Moreover, we demonstrate that the generalised Gibbs state for all three cases contains a non-commutation term, which has not been previously considered.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel framework for understanding the Lindblad master equation without assumptions, highlighting the importance of generalized charges and their effects on quantum dynamics.
AI.motivation: To explore the dynamics of open quantum systems without the typical limitations, providing a fresh perspective on the Lindblad master equation.
AI.method: The authors analyze the Lindblad (GKLS) master equation without prior assumptions, decomposing quantum dynamics into free evolution, exchanges of generalized charges, and pure dephasing.
AI.result: The approach reveals that strong coupling, particle exchange, and non-Abelian effects stem from a common physical foundation, and introduces a non-commutation term in the generalized Gibbs state that has been overlooked in previous studies.
AI.conclusion: This work extends the understanding of quantum dynamics in open systems by integrating physical processes and providing new insights into the role of generalized charges.

title: Dilaton-Flattened Axion Inflation
summary: We present a solvable same-sector effective theory for anomaly-inspired axion inflation, in which a heavy trace-anomaly mode dynamically backreacts on the axion potential. The tree-level elimination of the radial field resums the backreaction into a closed-form Lambert-$W$ potential, naturally flattening the hilltop potential without external plateau operators. By deriving the exact trough metric, we evaluate all the observables on the fully reduced one-field action, bypassing uncontrolled kinetic approximations. Calibrated at $N_\star=56$, reheating-compatible branches yield $r\simeq0.033$--$0.036$ and $α_s\simeq-(4.6$--$4.7)\times10^{-4}$, comfortably satisfying the current ACT/SPT/BICEP constraints. The evolution remains strictly adiabatic ($m_\perp^2/H^2\gtrsim6.1$, $Ω/H\lesssim7.6\times10^{-4}$) with negligible sound-speed and metric corrections. We provide analytic control over the constant-$w_{\rm eff}$ reheating map, the $N_{\rm re}=0$ boundary, and robustness against vacuum-offset deformations. This Lambert-$W$ backbone establishes a precise, deformable benchmark for confining axion inflation, with microscopic matching and reheating microphysics accessible as systematic EFT refinements.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel effective theory for axion inflation using a Lambert-$W$ potential to simplify the dynamics and satisfy observational constraints.
AI.motivation: To develop a solvable model for axion inflation that effectively incorporates anomalies without relying on external operators.
AI.method: The authors eliminate the radial field at tree-level, leading to a Lambert-$W$ potential that flattens the inflationary potential. They derive observables from a reduced one-field action, ensuring robustness against approximations.
AI.result: The model yields consistent predictions for tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ and running of spectral index $α_s$, aligning with current observational constraints.
AI.conclusion: The Lambert-$W$ framework provides a flexible benchmark for axion inflation, offering pathways for further refinement and consistency with reheating physics.

title: Distributed Learning of Quantum State Tomography Robust to Readout Errors
summary: Scalable estimation of quantum states with readout errors is a central challenge in large multiqubit systems. Existing overlapping-tomography methods improve scalability by working with local subsystems, but they usually assume known or separately calibrated measurements. At the same time, readout-estimation methods model measurement errors without enforcing consistency among overlapping regional states. In this context, the present paper introduces a unified framework for joint regional quantum state tomography with readout errors. A multiqubit system is partitioned in overlapping regions, each region is assigned to a local density operator and a local confusion matrix, and neighboring regions are coupled through reduced-state consistency on shared subsystems. This leads to a structured bilinear optimization problem. To solve it, a distributed alternating method is developed in which the state-update step is handled by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), while the confusion-matrix updates are carried out locally in parallel. Analytical guarantees are also established, including a sufficient condition for local identifiability, local quadratic growth of the population misfit, and convergence of the inner state-update procedure. Simulations on Ring, Ladder, Torus, and Hub graph geometries show that joint estimation improves state recovery over fixed-readout reconstruction, recovers a substantial portion of oracle performance, and reveals a clear tradeoff between state estimation performance, communication, and computation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified framework for scalable quantum state estimation with readout errors, improving on existing methods by enforcing consistency among overlapping regions.
AI.motivation: The challenge of estimating quantum states accurately in large multiqubit systems, particularly considering readout errors and measurement consistency, prompts the need for improved methods.
AI.method: The framework partitions a multiqubit system into overlapping regions, assigning local density operators and confusion matrices, coupled through consistent reduced states. A distributed alternating method using ADMM for state updates is developed.
AI.result: The proposed method shows improved state recovery and approaches oracle performance in simulations, highlighting a tradeoff between estimation accuracy, communication, and computation requirements.
AI.conclusion: The approach enhances joint regional quantum state tomography, addressing scalability and consistency in estimating quantum states.

title: Echoes of Global Cosmic Strings
summary: If the Universe underwent a cosmic phase transition, it may have left behind a network of cosmic strings. When these strings arise from the breaking of a gauge symmetry, their decay produces a significant stochastic background of gravitational waves. In contrast, if they originate from the breaking of a global symmetry, their decay predominantly yields Nambu-Goldstone bosons, which can persist as dark matter or dark radiation. In this work, we assess the detectability of this particle spectrum using a range of cosmological probes. We employ semi-numerical methods to estimate the resulting energy density and compute the associated matter power spectrum. We then compare these predictions with observations of the cosmic microwave background, Lyman-$α$ forest, large-scale structure surveys, and the UV luminosity function, thereby deriving constraints on the Nambu-Goldstone boson mass and the symmetry-breaking scale. Finally, we present projections for the sensitivity of upcoming cosmic microwave background missions.

AI.tldr: The study investigates the consequences of cosmic strings from phase transitions in the Universe, focusing on decay products such as gravitational waves and Nambu-Goldstone bosons, and assesses their detectability through cosmological probes.
AI.motivation: To understand the implications of cosmic strings formed during the Universe's phase transitions and how they might yield observable effects in the form of gravitational waves or dark matter.
AI.method: Semi-numerical methods are used to estimate the energy density and matter power spectrum resulting from decay events, followed by a comparison of these predictions with various cosmological observations.
AI.result: Derived constraints on the mass of Nambu-Goldstone bosons and the symmetry-breaking scale, informed by observations of the cosmic microwave background and other cosmic structures.
AI.conclusion: Projected sensitivity of future cosmic microwave background missions indicates potential for better detection and understanding of these phenomena.

title: Distributed Variational Quantum Linear Solver
summary: The Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS), a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving linear systems, faces a practical scalability bottleneck: the Linear Combination of Unitaries (LCU) decomposition requires O(L^2) circuit evaluations per optimizer iteration, where $L$ can grow as 4^n for n-qubit systems for the worst case scenario. We address this computational bottleneck through two complementary strategies. First, we present a distributed VQLS (D-VQLS) framework, built on NVIDIA CUDA-Q, that enables asynchronous, scalable distribution of the O(L^2) cost-function evaluations. Second, a fast Walsh--Hadamard transform (FWHT)-based Pauli decomposition with 1% coefficient thresholding curbs the exponential growth of LCU terms, reducing L from O}(2^n) to O(1) for n > 6 qubits and compressing the per-iteration circuit complexity from O(n * 4^n) to O(n) for sparse, structured matrices. For a 10-qubit tridiagonal Toeplitz system, this yields a 256x reduction, from 23 million to 90,112 circuits per iteration, while preserving over $99.99\%$ solution fidelity. Additionally, to inform feasibility on early fault-tolerant QPUs, the paper provides resource estimates -- gate counts, qubit requirements, and circuit evaluations per iteration -- for VQLS applied to arbitrary matrices. The D-VQLS framework is validated on the NERSC Perlmutter supercomputer using multi-node, multi-GPU ideal state-vector simulations, achieving over 99.99% fidelity against classical solutions on tridiagonal Toeplitz and Hele--Shaw flow benchmarks, with near-ideal strong scaling up to 24 GPUs and 95.3% weak scaling efficiency at 96 GPUs processing 360,448 circuits per iteration for a 10-qubit system. Systematic profiling identifies the optimal resource allocation for distributed quantum circuit workloads, yielding a 2.52x speedup for the configurations studied.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a distributed framework to enhance the scalability of the Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS) by reducing circuit evaluation costs and computing complexity, achieving significant performance improvements for large quantum systems.
AI.motivation: To overcome the scalability bottleneck in the VQLS due to the high number of required circuit evaluations in Linear Combination of Unitaries (LCU) decomposition, especially as the number of qubits increases.
AI.method: A distributed VQLS (D-VQLS) framework leveraging NVIDIA CUDA-Q is introduced for scalable asynchronous distribution of circuit evaluations, along with a fast Walsh--Hadamard transform-based Pauli decomposition to reduce the complexity of LCU terms.
AI.result: Achieved a 256x reduction in circuit evaluations per iteration for a 10-qubit system while preserving over 99.99% solution fidelity, demonstrating effective scaling on multi-GPU systems with significant speedup.
AI.conclusion: The D-VQLS framework substantially improves the scalability and efficiency of VQLS for large quantum systems, validated through simulations that confirm high fidelity and computational efficiency.

title: Performance Optimization Method for Laser-Phase-Noise based Quantum Random Number Generation
summary: The quantum random number generation based on laser phase noise, which is featured with high generation rate and ease for photonic integration, has been extensively investigated and demonstrated. Despite these advancements, a theoretical model to achieve optimal performance in terms of maximizing the generation rate or entropy is still incomplete. In this work, a comprehensive physical model for this scheme is introduced to accurately predict the power spectrum and probability distribution of raw data, based on which the entropy source bandwidth and quantum min-entropy can be accordingly calculated and thus the system performance can be quantitatively evaluated. The model is sufficiently validated through both simulation and experiment with significant agreement under various setups. Furthermore, our proposal enables the priori configuration of experimental setups to achieve designed power spectrum and probability distribution of the raw data, thereby maximizing the generation rate or the min-entropy for system performance optimization.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive model for quantum random number generation based on laser phase noise, aiming to optimize performance metrics like generation rate and entropy.
AI.motivation: Despite advancements in quantum random number generation, a theoretical model for optimal performance has been lacking.
AI.method: The paper introduces a physical model to predict the power spectrum and probability distribution of raw data, enabling calculation of entropy source bandwidth and quantum min-entropy.
AI.result: The model was validated through simulations and experiments, showing significant agreement in various setups.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model allows for the design of experimental configurations to maximize generation rates or min-entropy, optimizing system performance.

title: Dual-mode ground-state cooling in quadratic optomechanical systems: from multistability to general dark-mode suppression
summary: We theoretically investigate a quadratic optomechanical system comprising a single-mode optical cavity linearly coupled to one mechanical resonator and quadratically coupled to a second resonator. By tuning the cavity detuning and optomechanical coupling strengths, we demonstrate the transition from optical bistability to multistability with up to seven steady-state solutions. Notably, simultaneous ground-state cooling of both mechanical resonators occurs on the dynamically stable branch of the nonlinear steady-state solutions, offering new opportunities for combined nonlinear optical and quantum cooling functionalities. Beyond the multistable regime, we systematically study dual-mode ground-state cooling and find that robust simultaneous cooling can be achieved over a broad parameter range, except when the linear and quadratic couplings become comparable, where a dark-mode effect arises. In this case, tuning the second-order optomechanical-induced frequency shifts effectively suppresses dark-mode interference, enabling controllable and simultaneous ground-state cooling. Our results provide a versatile framework for engineering multimode quantum states in optomechanical systems and open new avenues for the development of multifunctional quantum devices, including ultra-sensitive sensors, scalable quantum memories, and integrated quantum networks.

AI.tldr: This study explores a quadratic optomechanical system, revealing a transition to multistability and enabling dual-mode ground-state cooling.
AI.motivation: To investigate the dynamics of a quadratic optomechanical system and enhance functionalities related to quantum cooling and nonlinear optical behaviors.
AI.method: The authors analyze a system with a single-mode optical cavity and two mechanical resonators with different coupling strengths, mapping regions of bistability and multistability through parameter tuning.
AI.result: They achieve multistability with up to seven steady-state solutions and demonstrate robust simultaneous ground-state cooling across a wide parameter range, although challenges arise near comparable couplings due to dark-mode effects.
AI.conclusion: The findings offer a framework for engineering multimode quantum states and suggest applications in sensitive sensors, quantum memories, and networks.

title: General Static Solutions of the SU(2) Yang-Mills Equations from a Spin Vector Potential
summary: We present a systematic study of static solutions to the source-free SU(2) Yang-Mills equations, in which the gauge potential explicitly depends on spin operators. By employing the \emph{vector potential extraction approach} (VPEA) -- which requires the total angular momentum operator (orbital plus spin) to satisfy the standard angular momentum algebra -- we derive the most general form of the spin vector potential. This leads to the static ansatz $\{ \vec{A} = [k_1(\hat{r}\times\vecΓ) + k_2\vecΓ + k_3(\vecΓ\cdot\hat{r})\hat{r}]/r, \varphi = f_1(r)\,(\vecΓ\cdot\hat{r}) + f_2(r)\}$, parametrized by three constants $\{k_1, k_2, k_3\}$ and two radial functions $\{f_1(r), f_2(r)\}$. Substituting this ansatz into the Yang-Mills equations and imposing the angular momentum constraints from the VPEA yields a set of consistency equations. Solving these equations provides a complete classification of static solutions, including both real and complex families. Known simple SU(2) static solutions are recovered as special cases. Our classification reveals new static configurations that could be valuable for non-perturbative studies and for models where spin degrees of freedom couple to non-Abelian gauge fields.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates static solutions of SU(2) Yang-Mills equations with gauge potential dependence on spin operators, using a vector potential extraction method to classify various solutions.
AI.motivation: To explore static solutions of SU(2) Yang-Mills equations that involve spin, enhancing understanding of non-Abelian gauge fields and their configurations.
AI.method: Utilizing the vector potential extraction approach (VPEA) to derive a general spin vector potential ansatz, followed by substituting it into the Yang-Mills equations and applying angular momentum constraints to obtain consistency equations.
AI.result: A complete classification of static solutions to the Yang-Mills equations is achieved, uncovering new static configurations beyond known solutions.
AI.conclusion: This study provides valuable insights for non-perturbative analyses and interactions between spin and non-Abelian gauge fields.

title: Linear Optical Schemes to Postselect High-Dimensional Dicke States
summary: Multipartite entanglement is an essential quantum resource for various distributed quantum applications. One promising method for preparing multipartite entanglement is to interfere independent photons at linear optical interference setups. While heralding the successful interference and thereby the state generation is often costly, postselecting entangled states provides an achievable alternative in this framework. We introduce a family of interference schemes for postselecting symmetric qudit Dicke states, useful resources in quantum communication and variational quantum computing. We present schemes with and without ancillary photons and show that using ancillary photons can exceed the upper bound on the success probability of schemes without ancillary photons. Our results accommodate a wide range of linear optical schemes, providing multiple viable approaches for postselecting Dicke states.

AI.tldr: The paper presents interference schemes for postselecting symmetric qudit Dicke states in linear optical setups, improving success probability using ancillary photons.
AI.motivation: To efficiently create multipartite entanglement for distributed quantum applications, particularly using linear optical interference.
AI.method: Introduces a family of interference schemes for postselecting symmetric qudit Dicke states, both with and without ancillary photons.
AI.result: Demonstrates that schemes using ancillary photons can achieve higher success probabilities compared to those without, accommodating various linear optical configurations.
AI.conclusion: Multiple practical approaches are provided for postselecting Dicke states, enhancing resource creation for quantum communication and computing.

title: Observation of Tunable Superradiant Frequency Combs
summary: Cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light-matter interactions and exploring collective phenomena. In particular, superradiance, arising from collective quantum interference among emitters, has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled to an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-QED model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder, and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems exhibiting both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and optical domains. Our results not only open new avenues for dual-rail frequency-comb applications in quantum metrology and information processing, but also establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal as a novel nonequilibrium phase in driven open systems.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates dynamical phase transitions in cavity QED and introduces a model for periodic pulsed superradiance, paving the way for applications in quantum metrology.
AI.motivation: To explore the engineering of time-domain superradiance for applications like pulsed sources and frequency combs, which have not been thoroughly investigated.
AI.method: A driven-dissipative cavity-QED model was introduced to analyze the dynamics of a spin ensemble coupled to a superconducting resonator, revealing a transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiance.
AI.result: The study uncovers dynamical phases in superradiant emission and demonstrates that rare-earth ion spin systems can achieve phase-synchronized dual-rail superradiant frequency combs.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish a connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and new nonequilibrium phases, suggesting implications for quantum metrology and information processing.

title: Optimal Quantum Logarithmic Trace Inequality
summary: We establish a sharp logarithmic trace inequality that strengthens recent bounds of Cheng et al.(arXiv:2507.07961) by replacing their prefactor $c_s/s$ with the strictly smaller constant $G_s$. The constant $G_s$ is defined via the scalar inequality $\log(1+r)\le G_s r^s$ and admits a closed-form expression in terms of the Lambert $W$ function. Our approach introduces an iterative integration-by-parts procedure that lifts optimal scalar bounds to the operator level without loss. We prove that $G_s$ is the optimal universal constant, in the sense that no smaller constant satisfies the inequality for all positive operators. For density matrices, this optimality persists up to $s\le \frac{1}{2\log(2)}$, while beyond this threshold the commuting case exhibits a strictly smaller optimal constant and the noncommuting case remains open. In the regime $s\to0$, our result improves the prefactor $c_s/s$ of Cheng et al. by a factor of $1/e$. These sharper inequalities enhance key primitives in quantum information theory, including decoupling, convex-splitting, and covering lemmas, leading to tighter finite-resource bounds.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a refined logarithmic trace inequality with a smaller constant, enhancing previous results and demonstrating its optimality for positive operators.
AI.motivation: To improve previous bounds on logarithmic trace inequalities in quantum information theory.
AI.method: Introduces an iterative integration-by-parts procedure to enhance scalar bounds at the operator level, defining a new constant G_s via the Lambert W function.
AI.result: The paper proves that G_s is the optimal universal constant for the logarithmic trace inequality, with specific conditions under which this optimality holds for density matrices.
AI.conclusion: The resulting inequalities provide significant improvements for various primitives in quantum information theory, fostering tighter resource bounds.

title: Photonic state engineering via energy-level crossing by giant atoms in topological waveguide QED setup
summary: Photonic state engineering in waveguide QED is typically based on local light-matter interactions. This limits its control over the spatial structure of bound photonic states. Here, we demonstrate a distinct mechanism arising from the interplay between nonlocal giant-atom coupling and topological band structure. Specifically, we consider giant atoms coupled to a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger waveguide and show that this configuration enables a controllable energy-level crossing protected by the topological gap. Adiabatically sweeping the atomic detuning across the crossing leads to a controlled exchange between distinct photonic bound states. In a two-giant-atom configuration, this mechanism achieves high-fidelity conversion of a spatially splitting state into a combining state. Extending this scheme to three-giant atoms, we further realize robust, shape-preserving photon transfer mediated by sequential in-gap crossings. Our results demonstrate how topology and nonlocal light-matter coupling can be combined to achieve programmable control of bound photonic states in waveguide QED platforms.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a mechanism in waveguide quantum electrodynamics that combines nonlocal giant-atom coupling with topological band structures to control photonic bound states.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations in controlling the spatial structure of bound photonic states in waveguide QED, primarily tied to local light-matter interactions.
AI.method: The authors examine giant atoms coupled to a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger waveguide, leading to controllable energy-level crossings protected by a topological gap, facilitating the exchange of distinct photonic bound states through adiabatic detuning.
AI.result: The mechanism enables high-fidelity conversion of splitting states into combining states with two giant atoms and achieves robust photon transfer in a configuration with three giant atoms, utilizing sequential in-gap crossings to preserve the shape of the emitted states.
AI.conclusion: Combining topology with nonlocal light-matter coupling allows for programmable control of bound photonic states in waveguide QED systems.

title: Spectroscopic measurement of the Casimir-Polder force in the intermediate regime
summary: The Casimir-Polder (CP) effect -- the force between a neutral atom and an uncharged conducting plate in empty space -- is an intriguing consequence of quantum vacuum fluctuations. The typically attractive CP potential crosses over from a scaling of $z^{-3}$ at short separations to $z^{-4}$ at long distances, where retardation effects due to the finite speed of light become important. At intermediate distances, where the atom--surface separation is of the order of the wavelength of the dominant atomic transition, experiments have so far relied on indirect methods, such as diffraction or quantum reflection, to observe the CP effect. Here, we directly reveal the CP force between strontium atoms and a dielectric surface via the induced shifts in the atomic energy levels in the intermediate regime. We spectroscopically probe the CP-induced kHz-frequency shift of ultracold atoms confined by a magic-wavelength optical lattice at 189(2)~nm from the surface -- on the scale of the dominant 461-nm transition. Our measurements agree well with QED calculations and differ from the short-range approximation, while excluding the long-distance one. This paves the way for studying the CP effect across various surface properties and geometries, as well as exploring the tensor nature of the atom-surface potential -- all important for the development of hybrid atomic optical-magnetic quantum devices.

AI.tldr: Direct measurement of the Casimir-Polder effect between strontium atoms and a dielectric surface using atomic energy level shifts reveals new insights into the nature of quantum forces at intermediate distances.
AI.motivation: Understanding the Casimir-Polder effect is key for advancements in quantum technologies and atomic physics, particularly in how neutral atoms interact with surfaces.
AI.method: The study used spectroscopic probing to measure the CP-induced frequency shifts in ultracold strontium atoms near a dielectric surface, specifically at a distance of 189 nm, investigating effects related to the atomic transition wavelength.
AI.result: The results aligned with quantum electrodynamics (QED) predictions and confirmed a discrepancy with short-range approximations, while also ruling out long-range models.
AI.conclusion: This research opens avenues for further exploration of the CP effect in relation to different surface characteristics and geometries, impacting future atomic quantum device development.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect in Non-Equilibrium Quantum Thermometry
summary: The quantum Mpemba effect (QMpE) describes an anomalous thermalization phenomenon in which quantum states initially far from equilibrium can approach thermal equilibrium faster than states that begin closer to it. While this effect has been extensively studied in various frameworks, its practical implications for quantum information processing remain largely unexplored. We investigate the relationship between QMpE and quantum thermometry, focusing on non-equilibrium scenarios where measurements are performed during early-stage thermalization. In a Markovian model, we rigorously prove that the initial states that are optimal for thermometry exhibit QMpE with high probability and thermalize faster than most initial states. Our results reveal a fundamental connection between quantum thermodynamics and thermometry, suggesting that QMpE can be harnessed to enhance temperature estimation with quantum probes.

AI.tldr: The quantum Mpemba effect (QMpE) reveals that certain quantum states can reach thermal equilibrium faster than those closer to equilibrium. This study links QMpE to quantum thermometry, demonstrating that optimal initial states for temperature measurement exhibit QMpE, potentially improving temperature estimation.
AI.motivation: To explore the largely unexplored implications of QMpE for quantum information processing and thermometry.
AI.method: A Markovian model was used to rigorously prove that initial states optimal for thermometry also exhibit QMpE with high probability and thermalize more rapidly.
AI.result: Initial states optimal for thermometry were shown to demonstrate QMpE and thermalize faster than most other states.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish a significant link between quantum thermodynamics and thermometry, indicating that QMpE can be utilized to enhance temperature estimation using quantum probes.

title: Activating entanglement and EPR steering from continuous-variable resources using witness-based measures
summary: We introduce a general witness-based framework for quantifying and operationally activating continuous-variable (CV) resources into discrete-variable (DV) bipartite entanglement or Einstein- Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering. For the three standard CV resource theories associated with Wigner negativity (WN), genuine non-Gaussianity (GNG), and standard non-Gaussianity (SNG), we define infinite families of bounded-witness monotones indexed by box constraints on the witness operators. For closed convex free sets, these monotones are faithful, strongly monotonic under free instruments, Lipschitz continuous, and convex. For closed nonconvex free sets, we show that faithfulness requires a two-copy lift and formulate the corresponding strong-monotonicity statement in the lifted theory. We further construct witness-dependent completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) measure-and-prepare channels whose outputs are two-qubit Werner states. For the representative case n = m = 1, the optimal entanglement and EPR steering attainable within this witness-dependent activation family are exactly proportional to the underlying monotones. We illustrate the framework with odd-parity states, pure-loss single-photon states, and Gottesman- Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, and derive explicit lower bounds for pure-state GNG and SNG. More broadly, our results show that closed CV free sets admit witness-based quantifiers with a direct operational interpretation in terms of experimentally accessible DV correlations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a framework for converting continuous-variable (CV) resources into discrete-variable (DV) entanglement and EPR steering, defining witness monotones for CV resource theories and establishing operational connections with experimental correlations.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic approach for quantifying and activating CV resources into DV entanglement or EPR steering, enhancing operational understanding and applicability in quantum resource theories.
AI.method: A general witness-based framework is introduced, characterized by bounded-witness monotones under specific constraints. The authors establish properties like faithfulness, strong monotonicity, and continuity for both convex and non-convex free sets, and construct CPTP channels leading to two-qubit Werner states.
AI.result: The framework reveals that the optimal entanglement and EPR steering obtained from witness-dependent activations depend directly on underlying monotones, with specific examples illustrating these results.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that CV free sets can be effectively quantified and operationalized through witness-based methods, offering clear pathways for translating CV resources into experimentally relevant DV correlations.

title: Integrable, Mixed, and Chaotic Dynamics in a Single All-to-All Ising Spin Model
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures. Accepted in Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
summary: We demonstrate that the Ising all-to-all (ATA) model exhibits a range of dynamics, from integrable to chaotic, including mixed behaviour across symmetry blocks within a single system. While other works have explored the dynamics of all-to-all systems by varying parameters, we analyse a fixed set of parameters and examine the dynamics within different blocks. In addition to investigating the dynamical properties, we show that the system remains resilient to noise when the norm of the Hamiltonian representing the noise is close to 1. Our results are presented by mapping each symmetry sector of the system to a kicked top (KT) and observing that KT parameters for each sector depend on its dimension. This system, similar to the Bunimovich billiard for classical chaos, provides a new platform for studying dynamics determined by the symmetry sector, advancing quantum chaos research.

AI.tldr: The Ising all-to-all model displays a spectrum of dynamics, from integrable to chaotic, resilient to noise, and linked to symmetry sectors via kicked top dynamics.
AI.motivation: To explore the dynamics of the Ising ATA model and its resilience to noise while considering fixed parameters.
AI.method: Dynamics are analyzed across symmetry blocks, with each block mapped to a kicked top; the dependence of KT parameters on block dimension is examined.
AI.result: The study reveals varied dynamics across blocks and confirms noise resilience when the Hamiltonian norm approaches 1; the mapping to kicked tops elucidates these findings.
AI.conclusion: The findings create a new basis for understanding quantum chaos, analogous to classical chaos in the Bunimovich billiard, enhancing research into symmetry sector dynamics.

title: Coherence dynamics in quantum algorithm for linear systems of equations
summary: Quantum coherence is a fundamental issue in quantum mechanics and quantum information processing. We explore the coherence dynamics of the evolved states in HHL quantum algorithm for solving the linear system of equation $A\overrightarrow{x}=\overrightarrow{b}$. By using the Tsallis relative $α$ entropy of coherence and the $l_{1,p}$ norm of coherence, we show that the operator coherence of the phase estimation $P$ relies on the coefficients $β_{i}$ obtained by decomposing $|b\rangle$ in the eigenbasis of $A$. We prove that the operator coherence of the inverse phase estimation $\widetilde{P}$ relies on the coefficients $β_{i}$, eigenvalues of $A$ and the success probability $P_{s}$, and it decreases with the increase of the probability when $α\in(1,2]$. Moreover, the variations of coherence deplete with the increase of the success probability and rely on the eigenvalues of $A$ as well as the success probability.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the dynamics of quantum coherence in the HHL quantum algorithm for linear equations, emphasizing how coherence depends on certain coefficients and probabilities.
AI.motivation: To understand the coherence dynamics inherent in the HHL quantum algorithm, which is essential for quantum computing applications in solving linear systems.
AI.method: Utilizing Tsallis relative α entropy and l_{1,p} norm of coherence to analyze coherence for the phase estimation and inverse phase estimation processes.
AI.result: The research shows that coherence is influenced by coefficients from the eigenbasis decomposition and the success probability, with specific patterns based on the value of α.
AI.conclusion: As success probability increases, coherence decreases, indicating a relationship between coherence depletion, eigenvalues of A, and probability measures.

title: Time-Dependent Logarithmic Perturbation Theory for Quantum Dynamics: Formulation and Applications
summary: We present a time-dependent extension of logarithmic perturbation theory for nonrelativistic quantum dynamics governed by the Schrödinger equation, in which the logarithm of the wave function is expanded in powers of a coupling constant. The resulting hierarchy of equations defining the perturbative corrections is governed by a gauge-rotated Hamiltonian of the unperturbed system and leads to closed-integral expressions for the time-dependent corrections based on Duhamel's formula. This closed-integral structure of corrections is a hallmark of time-independent logarithmic perturbation theory and is preserved in the present extension. This structure, in particular, provides a computable expression for the instantaneous energy shift. Furthermore, dynamic energy shifts arise naturally within this framework in the form of time-averaged expectation values of pseudopotentials and can be related, for example, to AC Stark shifts and electric polarizabilities. As an illustration, we apply the method to the harmonic oscillator and the hydrogen atom, both driven by a time-dependent laser field. The harmonic oscillator provides a proof of principle for which the exact solution is recovered, while the hydrogen atom illustrates the method applied to atomic systems. Supported by numerical simulations, we demonstrate the applicability to obtain relevant physical observables with high accuracy. The present approach offers a promising alternative for analytical studies of time-dependent multi-photon processes in the perturbative regime.

AI.tldr: This paper extends logarithmic perturbation theory to time-dependent nonrelativistic quantum dynamics, providing a framework for calculating corrections to wave functions and energy shifts influenced by external fields, applicable to systems like the harmonic oscillator and hydrogen atom.
AI.motivation: To develop a method that handles time-dependent quantum systems accurately while preserving the structure of logarithmic perturbation theory.
AI.method: The authors expand the logarithm of the wave function in powers of a coupling constant, resulting in a hierarchy of equations governed by a gauge-rotated Hamiltonian and yielding closed-integral expressions for time-dependent corrections based on Duhamel's formula.
AI.result: The method successfully applies to the harmonic oscillator and hydrogen atom, recovering exact solutions and yielding accurate numerical simulations of energy shifts related to time-dependent external fields.
AI.conclusion: This revised approach offers an effective framework for studying time-dependent multi-photon processes in quantum systems, demonstrating high accuracy in calculating relevant physical observables.

title: Quantum Thermometry of External Phonon Reservoirs in Driven Open Quantum Systems
summary: We investigate the non-monotonic temperature sensitivity of a coherently driven two-level quantum system coupled to an Ohmic phonon environment. By employing a unitary polaron transformation, we account for phonon-induced renormalization effects that go beyond the standard weak-coupling approximations. Our analysis reveals that the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) exhibits a prominent peak at an intermediate system-environment coupling strength, identifying an optimal regime for thermal sensing. This behavior emerges from a fundamental competition between environment-induced dissipation enhancement and the exponential suppression of system parameters due to phonon dressing. We demonstrate that while thermometric precision vanishes in both the ultra-weak and strong coupling limits, a properly tuned nonequilibrium steady state can significantly enhance sensitivity. These results suggest that environmental interactions, often viewed as detrimental decoherence sources, can be engineered as a resource to optimize the performance of solid-state quantum thermometers.

AI.tldr: The paper studies temperature sensitivity in a two-level quantum system influenced by phonon environments, finding an optimal coupling strength that enhances thermal sensing.
AI.motivation: To explore how environmental interactions affect the temperature sensitivity of quantum systems, particularly in the context of enhancing thermometric precision.
AI.method: The study employs a unitary polaron transformation to analyze phonon-induced renormalization effects beyond weak-coupling approximations, focusing on Quantum Fisher Information (QFI).
AI.result: The QFI shows a peak at intermediate coupling strengths, indicating an optimal regime for thermal sensing, while thermometric precision diminishes at weak and strong coupling limits.
AI.conclusion: Environmental interactions can be harnessed to improve the performance of quantum thermometers, transforming potential decoherence sources into advantages for thermal sensitivity.

title: Split-Evolution Quantum Phase Estimation for Particle-Conserving Hamiltonians
summary: We present a hardware demonstration and resource analysis of split-evolution quantum phase estimation (SE-QPE) on a Quantinuum System Model H2 quantum computer. SE-QPE is a modification to canonical QPE for particle-conserving Hamiltonians in which controlled time evolution is replaced by CSWAP-based interference between a target register and a reference register. For factorizations of time evolution with a shared eigenbasis, SE-QPE preserves the phase-register outcome distribution of canonical QPE and, unlike with compute--uncompute substitutions, it remains compatible with non-exact eigenstates. The substitution removes controlled-simulation overhead and enables parallel evolution on two registers, reducing the depth of each phase-kickback block. Resource analysis for Trotterized double-factorized chemistry Hamiltonians shows that the substitution becomes increasingly favorable at higher phase powers, as such combining QPE and SE-QPE implementations can be a useful option. Over a range of FeMoco active spaces, SE-QPE reduces time evolution resources, with asymptotic reductions of about 33% in CX count, 25% in $T$ count, and an asymptotic depth ratio of $3/N$ for CX layers. On Quantinuum H2-2, a four-qubit model ethylene demonstration with explicit inverse QFT and repeated phase-kickback steps up to 6 phase bits yields distinct energies and shows the auxiliary registers provide useful error detection filters.

AI.tldr: The paper showcases SE-QPE, a quantum phase estimation method that improves efficiency in quantum computing. It presents a hardware demonstration on a specific quantum computer, emphasizing reduced resource requirements in evolution processes, particularly for complex Hamiltonians.
AI.motivation: To enhance the efficiency of quantum phase estimation while preserving compatibility with non-exact eigenstates and reducing controlled simulation overhead.
AI.method: SE-QPE modifies canonical quantum phase estimation by using CSWAP-based interference instead of controlled time evolution, allowing for parallel evolution and resource reduction in Hamiltonians with shared eigenbases.
AI.result: SE-QPE achieves up to 33% reduction in CX count, 25% in $T$ count, and an asymptotic depth ratio of $3/N$ for CX layers, demonstrating significant resource savings over various FeMoco active spaces.
AI.conclusion: SE-QPE demonstrates a valuable approach for reducing resource demands in quantum phase estimation, particularly beneficial for high-phase power applications, and provides useful error detection capabilities in quantum computations.

title: Learning to Concatenate Quantum Codes
summary: Concatenating quantum error correction codes scales error correction capability by driving logical error rates down double-exponentially across levels. However, the noise structure shifts under concatenation, making it hard to choose an optimal code sequence.
